transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. It's really nice to meet you too. Thank you so much for fitting me in. 

Um, I guess... well, I hope I'm explaining this right, but what really brought me in is that my mind just won't stay on one thing anymore. I'm sure it's probably not a huge deal, but it's been affecting my work a little bit. I'm a jeweler, and lately at the bench, I'll just jump from a customer email... to a saw mark on a piece of metal... to a noise outside... and then I realize I’ve completely lost track of the whole work order. 

I'm usually a really good worker, I promise, and I always try to stay on top of things. It's just been a bit scattered lately. Does that make sense? Is that the kind of thing you need to know?
Have you struggled with this kind of difficulty staying focused your entire life, or is this something that has only started happening recently?

Oh, no, definitely not my whole life. I promise I'm usually a really reliable person and I can concentrate just fine. 

Um... this really just started recently. It was right after this jewelry show... I actually won an award, which was amazing, but... well, right after that, I got into this really wired stretch. I hope it doesn't make me sound irresponsible, but it just got a little out of control, and that went on for about two weeks. I just couldn't rein my brain in at all during that time. 

Does that make sense? I hope I'm giving you the right kind of information, I just want to make sure I'm answering your questions properly.
During that two-week period when you felt so wired, did you find that you were able to get by with much less sleep than you usually need?

Um, yeah, I guess I was. But it really wasn't a bad thing, I promise! I hope it doesn't sound like I was neglecting my health or anything, because I usually try really hard to take good care of myself. It's just that... well, for a while there, I was only sleeping maybe two or three hours a night. 

But I wasn't exhausted at all. I would wake up completely clear-headed. I was just so excited to get to work, you know? I'd be up way before sunrise, already at my bench cutting stones or taking pictures to post new designs online. I was actually getting so much done for my business, so it felt really positive at the time. 

I hope that doesn't make me sound too strange. Is that the kind of detail you were looking for? I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need.

During those two weeks, was your behavior so out of character or intense that it caused significant problems in your personal life or work, or did it reach the point where you needed to be hospitalized?

Oh, no, definitely no hospitals! I promise it wasn't anything scary like that. I would never let things get that far out of hand. 

Um... but I guess, well, it did cause a little bit of a hiccup. I hate to even admit this, because I really pride myself on my customer service, but... I actually ended up missing a major custom delivery. And I guess my shop records just got so disorganized that I've had to stop taking new work for right now. Just until I can catch up, you know? I'm usually so responsible with my business, I promise I'm going to get it all sorted out and back to normal. 

And, well, my family has been checking on me a bit more, too. I think they just got a little worried because they saw how far I’d slipped from my usual routines. But we're all okay! I just... I hope you don't think I'm a failure or a bad business owner for letting things slide like that. Does that answer your question? I hope I'm giving you the right details.
During those two weeks when you were sleeping so little and working so intensely, did you feel unusually happy, euphoric, or perhaps irritable and easily angered?

Um, well... I definitely wouldn't say I was angry. I'm usually a really easygoing guy, I promise. I try really hard to get along with everyone. 

But I guess... well, right after the show, I just felt so, I don't know, lit up? Like I was larger than life and everything was just clicking perfectly. It was a really great feeling, actually. But, um, I suppose I did get a little bit... frustrated? Just a tiny bit, when people would tell me I needed to stick to my normal shop hours or tell me to slow down. I might have snapped at them just a little. 

I feel terrible about it now, because I know they were just trying to help. I really don't like being short with people. I hope that doesn't make me sound like a mean person, because I'm really not. I just had so much momentum going. Does that make sense? Is that the kind of thing you were asking about?

During that time, did you ever feel that your thoughts were racing so fast that you couldn't keep up with them, or did you ever feel like you were so energized that you were doing things that were clearly risky or out of character for you?

Um, no, I wouldn't say my thoughts were racing or anything like that. I mean, I was definitely focused and had a lot of ideas for my jewelry, but my mind felt really clear, I promise. I was just being creative, you know? 

And as for doing risky things... no, definitely not. I'm a really careful person, especially with my business and my finances. I don't like taking big chances or doing things that are out of character. I just wanted to make the most of the inspiration I had at the time. I hope it doesn't sound like I was acting crazy or being irresponsible, because I really try my best to be sensible. Does that sound okay? I just want to make sure I'm answering your questions the right way.
